purpose: Brodalumab is used to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults when other treatments have not worked well enough. It helps clear up the red, scaly, itchy patches on the skin caused by psoriasis. It is only used when the benefits outweigh the risks, and it is not a cure, but it can greatly improve your skin and quality of life.
how_it_works: Your immune system makes a protein called interleukin-17A that causes the inflammation and skin changes seen in psoriasis. Brodalumab is an injectable medication that blocks the receptor your body uses to respond to this protein. By blocking that signal, it calms down the overactive immune response that causes those thick, scaly skin patches.
common_side_effects: Joint pain, tiredness, headache, diarrhea, nausea, fungal infections like thrush in the mouth or throat, and redness or pain at the injection site. You may also be more likely to pick up colds or other minor infections.
warnings: This medication carries a serious warning about suicidal thoughts and behavior, so it is only available through a special safety program called REMS. Tell your doctor right away if you feel depressed, have thoughts of hurting yourself, or notice big mood changes. Do not use this medication if you have Crohn's disease, as it may make it worse. Because it affects your immune system, it can increase your risk of serious infections, so let your doctor know if you have any signs of infection such as fever, chills, or unusual tiredness. Do not take live vaccines while using this medication.
typical_dosing: Brodalumab is given as an injection under the skin. The usual schedule is one injection (210 mg) once a week for the first three doses (at weeks 0, 1, and 2), and then one injection every two weeks after that. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to inject it at home using a prefilled autoinjector pen.
